defaults.permitted_development: Across Devon, driveway surfacing is often permitted development, but the easy route usually depends on drainage. If the area in front of the house and facing the highway exceeds 5 square metres, it should be permeable or direct run-off to a permeable part of the curtilage, and any dropped kerb is dealt with separately.

rules.height_rules: Across Devon, there is no standalone driveway height allowance. The planning risk usually comes from raised parking decks, retaining walls, steps, ramps or embankments rather than from the surface itself.
rules.depth_rules: Across Devon, no set driveway depth applies, but the parking space should work in practice: vehicles should be able to sit within the curtilage rather than project over the pavement. Tight frontage layouts often fail on useability before they fail on surfacing rules.
rules.boundary_rules: Across Devon, the surfacing can be permitted development while the boundary and access works are not. Enlarging the entrance, cutting back walls or crossing the public footway often needs a separate highways check and sometimes planning permission as well.
rules.roof_rules: Across Devon, there is no roof allowance for a driveway in itself. Any canopy, covered bay or car-port element proposed with the parking area needs to be checked as a separate structure.
rules.materials_rules: Across Devon, for front-of-house surfaces over 5 square metres, use permeable materials or drain run-off to a porous area within the curtilage. Permeable block paving, porous asphalt, resin-bound systems designed for infiltration or gravel with a suitable sub-base are usually easier to justify than impermeable paving draining to the highway.

restrictions.listed_building: Driveway works affecting a listed building, its curtilage, or historic boundary structures can need listed building consent as well as any planning or highway approval.

rules.permitted_development: In Exeter, most house driveways can proceed without a planning application where the work stays inside the curtilage and front-of-house surfacing over 5 square metres is permeable or drains to a porous area within the site.
